text:
Predicates:
Engaged(x) ::: x is engaged.
MakeWeddingPlans(x) ::: x makes wedding plans.
InviteOthers(x) ::: x invites others to come to their ceremony.
WellAttendedWedding(x) ::: x has a well-attended wedding.
LargerFamily(x) ::: x has a larger family.
Premises:
∀x (MakeWeddingPlans(x) → Engaged(x)) ::: All people who make wedding plans are people who are engaged.
∀x (InviteOthers(x) → MakeWeddingPlans(x)) ::: All people who invite others to come to their ceremony make wedding plans.
∀x (WellAttendedWedding(x) → InviteOthers(x)) ::: Anyone who has a well-attended wedding invites others to come to their ceremony.
∃x (WellAttendedWedding(x) ∧ LargerFamily(x)) ::: Some people that have well-attended weddings have larger families.
Engaged(john) → ¬(InviteOthers(john) ∧ MakeWeddingPlans(john)) ::: If John is engaged, then John does not invite friends to their ceremony and make wedding plans.
LargerFamily(john) → (WellAttendedWedding(john) ∨ InviteOthers(john)) ::: If John has a larger family, then either John has a well-attended wedding or invites friends to their ceremony.
Conclusion:
¬(LargerFamily(john) ∨ InviteOthers(john)) ::: John neither has a larger family nor does he invite others to his wedding.
